newsitem.title: FRANCE: French-treated nuclear waste heads back to Japan.
newsitem.headline: French-treated nuclear waste heads back to Japan.

text.p: A giant, 40-tonne load of processed nuclear waste was discreetly shipped by train overnight under heavy police guard to the French port of Cherbourg on its way back to Japan, French officials said on Friday.
The waste, initially sent from Japan to be reprocessed at the French nuclear reprocessing plant at La Hague in Normandy, was expected to be loaded on a double-hulled ship in the next few days.

The Greenpeace environmentalist group, which accuses authorities of suppressing information about movement of nuclear waste, said it believed the shipment would be taken back to Japan aboard the British cargo vessel Lean, expected in Cherbourg soon. It said the Lean would set sail on January 16.

Previous shipments to Japan and elsewhere have caused an outcry among anti-nuclear militants. Thousands of protesters battled police in Germany when one such shipment from France arrived there last May.
